photograph.file: Araignée mâle sur fond de maërl (Ifremer 00557-66908 - 20311).jpg
photograph.author: Olivier Dugornay
photograph.description: The Atlantic spider crab ( Maja brachydactyla ) is a crustacean. It is found in the waters of the North Sea to the Canaries, on sandy or rocky bottoms, between the surface and 50 m deep. Here, it is a male individual, photographed in the harbor of Brest on a bottom of maërl (accumulation of coralline algae common in Brittany). Its shell, strongly domed and rounded, can measure up to 25 cm long and 18 cm wide. Its legs, with significant hairiness, are long and thin. Note that, unlike other crustaceans, the spider crab has a terminal moult, which has the consequence of stopping its growth abruptly. Its fishing is subject to regulation: see Berne Convention (relating to the conservation of wildlife and natural habitats in Europe): Annex III – Protected species .

shape.before: The earlier withheld oval/rod-limbed draft is preserved on the body sheet.
shape.changed: A strongly convex pear-shaped shell with separate median/lateral tapered spines and paired divergent rostral horns, eight long articulated walking limbs, curved terminal toes and longer robust male chelipeds replaces the smooth oval with rods. Male arms now spread laterally instead of pointing together in front.
shape.remaining: Detailed orbital/hepatic spine clusters, antennal basal plates, maxillipeds, sternum, gonopods and appendage proportions remain incomplete or unmeasured. The shell and male palms still simplify the photo. Fine hair density, substrate cover and optical response are illustrative. Primary figure pixels could not be obtained in this access; no claim of figure-based geometric measurement is made.

sourceAssessment: The complete Plazi species-treatment HTML was retrieved, and Ng&Richer de Forges2015 selected diagnosis/figure captions were read. It distinguishes the current adult species from M.squinado and smaller more-spiny specimens. Zenodo PDF/figure downloads403 and a stalled browser reference page are recorded. The authentic Olivier Dugornay/Ifremer source-labelled male at Brest was actually compared, providing independent photographic shape context without a new taxon determination.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Lengthened and spread the male chelipeds, narrowed palm depth and lowered their finger orientation after frontal comparison.
Extended visible attached setae and retained separate tapered spines rather than round pegs.
Lifted the folded arms in quiet support after the geometry check detected floor penetration; final42 states captured after that correction.
